draftArchitecture.plainAnswer: An AI completion claim is useful only for the result its evidence actually establishes.
causalSequence: The reader needs a teammate to use a handout.
An assistant checking only that it made a file has evidence of creation.
Access depends separately on the sharing settings and intended recipient.
A file-existing result cannot by itself establish recipient access.
Check the particular outcome at the boundary where it happens; keep uncertainty visible.
draftArchitecture.workedCase: Clearly fictional assistant-created workshop handout: file exists, but a teammate may still be unable to open its link.
draftArchitecture.transferCase: A calendar event saved on your calendar does not by itself establish that the intended colleague received an invitation.
draftArchitecture.usefulAction: Name who needs to do what with the result; check with an intended recipient using existing permitted access, without making private files public.
draftArchitecture.formatSpecificStructure: Headline, short founder opening, labelled fictional example, causal explanation, one earned VHS comparison and a proportionate action. No attachments or new public product claims.
draftArchitecture.antiTemplateDecision: Do not reproduce the former draft’s internal four-state vocabulary or prompt; use a fresh ordinary collaboration example.

analogyPlan.concept: A description does not perform or prove its named action
analogyPlan.analogy: Be Kind, Rewind printed on a VHS case
analogyPlan.mapping: A rewind label can request an action while the tape stays at the end; a done label can name a result without checking it.
analogyPlan.limit: An AI assistant can perform real actions when equipped and authorized; the analogy concerns evidence, not all tool capability.
analogyPlan.whyItHelps: The familiar label makes the missing action easy to remember and reconnects immediately to the outcome check.

humourPlan.lessonJob: The rewind-label joke makes the difference between a label and the real result stick.
